mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad-based demand weakness, which amplifies recession risk and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the federal funds rate of 0.75% or more signals aggressive monetary tightening, which quickly raises borrowing costs and reduces investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative following a FEDFUNDS monthly increase of 0.75% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A positive interaction between payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) where PAYEMS growth is below 0.2% while UNRATE rises above 4% signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS growth < 0.2% and UNRATE > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for six consecutive months signals sustained consumer demand weakness, which erodes corporate revenues and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during any six-month period of consecutive monthly declines in RSAFS.
